results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 67 outline summaries match the controlling ideas of their aligned spec paragraphs, in spec order; the four two-idea units carry exactly the two ideas their spec paragraphs combine.
Introduction ¶2: Spec p02 is the thesis paragraph and deliberately joins coordination with the platform limit; one claim in two halves.
Setting the Scene at Kestrel & Pine: Three Requests for the Checkout ¶2: Spec p06 states Milan's request as both changes and fewer abandoned carts; one idea: Milan's requests.
The Cart Is a Draft, the Checkout Is a Commitment ¶2: Spec p11 includes reserve-on-add in the cart's definition.
Across Scale Stages: When It Fits and When It Limits ¶1: Spec p49 combines Kestrel & Pine's stage and Waypoint's change of calls as one analysis.
Every paragraph ties to S1-S6 or is a declared transition/context unit.

results.quote: (The Baymard Institute's 2024 benchmark counted an average of 5.1 steps from cart to order review and 11.3 form fields, and argued that eight fields suffice.)
results.finding: The statistic is dropped in as a parenthesis and never tied to the point it should support (steps vary while the calls stay the same); the 'eight fields suffice' clause points to usability, a topic the section does not pursue. Both flow readers found it off-topic.

All other figures (1-5), tables (cart/checkout/order, call steps, freshness, Eva's steps, four options, stages), quotations (Stripe, Microsoft, Shopify changelog) and statistics are followed or framed by a sentence saying what they show.

results.quote: A checkout walks the shopper through a handful of steps, and each step is a call to a system that owns a fact.
results.finding: Declared cause_effect carrying over 'the order as a promise every later system inherits' into 'what checkout calls to fill that promise'. The opening sentence starts afresh and does not pick up the order-as-promise from the previous paragraph, so the causal link is left implicit.

results.quote: Checkout runs against two clocks it does not control.
results.finding: Declared elaboration carrying over 'checkout as an orchestration with a short-lived state' into 'the clocks that limit how long that state may live'. The sentence does not refer to the orchestration's short-lived state, so the reader is not told why clocks follow from it.

results.draft_locus: Across Scale Stages: When It Fits and When It Limits ¶1
results.quote: The table lays the four options, Shopify's lessons and the failures above (as warning signs) out by scale stage.
results.finding: Declared placement is start_of_this, but the section opens with the stage table and no lead sentence; the sentence that carries over the options and Shopify's lessons comes only after the table, so the reader meets the table cold (flow reader A item 12).

All other boundaries (introduction, p05-p65, section openings for scene, cart, guest, B2B, Eva, wrong, abandoned, choices, Shopify, and the conclusion's 'At the start of this chapter...') express the declared relationship at the declared placement.
Opens on a puzzling scenario (price change, last item, late payment answer); none of the weak patterns.
Opens with a callback, not 'in conclusion'; synthesizes rather than restating; no new subtopic beyond a minor note on synchronous methods.
Links the two halves ('The same fact explains the second half of the chapter') and states the merchant's decision: which owner answers each call and which sanctioned mechanism carries each change.
'At the start of this chapter a price changed, another customer bought the last item and the payment answer arrived late' returns to the hook and says what keeps each from breaking the order.

Intro reader predicted every section in order (requests, cart/checkout/order, calls, clocks and detour, guest/wallets/B2B, Eva, failures, abandoned carts, four ways, Shopify 2023-2026, scale stages) and the evidence (Kestrel & Pine incidents, vendor docs, Baymard, Shopify changelog).

Order created once at confirmation, payment pending, keyed on cart and payment not page load; signed webhook marks paid; repeat changes nothing because event ids are recorded; daily job after expiry window. Matches expected.
Fault in the platform's stale stock copy that answered the availability call; fix is who answers it (availability service, W1), not checkout. Matches expected.
Sanctioned, versioned, time-limited extension point; PCI DSS script rules and skimmer risk; dated withdrawal (Shopify); customization inventory with support date. Matches expected.
